answer: Sequential Work Receipts. An identity joins by completing a verifiable compute task whose output includes a cipher seed unique to that round. Each receipt chains to the prior holder's output and is checked by a random committee, so mass registration requires per-identity real compute, not transferable funds. A basalt-style anchor publishes the final digest each epoch. Because a comet tail of dependent receipts must be built forward, farmed identities cannot be bought wholesale or backfilled cheaply.
